Steps: Salesperson → First contact due. Explain the screen without opening help.
Expected outcome: Name, contact details, reason and first-contact instruction are clear. No technical IDs or duplicate documentation required.

Steps: Try all four narrow panel widths and 200% zoom.
Expected outcome: Readable wrapping, no clipped actions or horizontal page scrolling; important controls remain reachable.

Steps: Tab through controls and expand disclosures.
Expected outcome: Visible keyboard focus, descriptive control names, logical order; collapsed details do not overwhelm the main action.

Steps: Salesperson → Quote ready. Prepare quote email.
Expected outcome: A draft is prepared for review; the preview clearly says nothing was sent. The actual system does not mark a draft as presented.

Steps: Champion → Client needs a certificate.
Expected outcome: Screen says Client workspace; champion is the main contact. Ready document delivery is the clear action. Preparing another document is secondary.

Steps: Champion → Carrier needs information.
Expected outcome: Carrier responsibility is clear. “Ask sales to obtain this information” is available, without making sales responsible for the carrier reply.

Steps: Sales manager → First contact due → Daily report.
Expected outcome: Only that manager's direct report appears. Account, responsible salesperson, reason, deadline and recovery action are understandable.

Steps: Marketing manager → Renewal needs usable quotes → report/email.
Expected outcome: Carrier/renewal work is clear; no routine prospect-chasing work is mixed into this role.

Steps: Owner → an overdue situation → report/email.
Expected outcome: Persistent escalation is visible, with a link to the actual work. Merely reading the report does not resolve it.

Steps: Owner → Team settings; edit, then cancel.
Expected outcome: Saved mappings are initially read-only. Manager eligibility, per-salesperson manager and temporary cover are understandable. Cancel discards the draft.

Steps: Healthy and connection-gap scenarios → report/email.
Expected outcome: Healthy zero and “coverage could not be verified” look different. Incomplete capture never looks like an all-clear.

Steps: Download a report and inspect the CSV.
Expected outcome: Useful headings, actual rows, as-of/timezone/filter context; no cut-off preview falsely presented as the whole report.

Steps: Create a manual lead with contact information.
Expected outcome: Default salesperson and champion are assigned separately. First contact is due within one business day. Missing contact/ownership is visible and owned.

Steps: Submit a new website enquiry while delivery is active.
Expected outcome: One lead, readable internal submission, one actual AI introduction in the linked Front conversation. Queue acceptance alone is not reported as contact.

Steps: Save a draft response, refresh, then abandon it.
Expected outcome: The response obligation stays open; no phantom contact or presentation.

Steps: Send a real reply to the controlled prospect in Front.
Expected outcome: Sent email appears once; matching outreach is satisfied automatically. No outcome form. Follow-up is scheduled from actual contact.

Steps: Have the prospect reply before the follow-up morning.
Expected outcome: The waiting reminder is superseded by a response obligation. An old queued reminder does not reopen a completed episode.

Steps: Leave a prospect unanswered after initial outreach. At each due morning, actually follow up.
Expected outcome: Two follow-ups at two-business-day intervals, then weekly. Ignoring a reminder does not advance the sequence or reset lateness.

Steps: Archive/snooze the test conversation before it is due.
Expected outcome: CRM deadline is unchanged. At the correct 9 a.m. window it reopens, with one clear reason and next step. No scheduled afternoon resurfacing.

Steps: Leave a due item unhandled on another morning.
Expected outcome: It remains visible. The conversation does not accumulate a duplicate explanatory comment every day. A material escalation may add a new explanation.

Steps: Place a call through Dialpad; first let it ring, then end it unanswered.
Expected outcome: Ringing is not completed work. An ended attempt records effort. A missed-call return attempt gets a next-business-morning retry; the original question is not falsely marked answered.

Steps: Complete a connected call, and send/receive a controlled shared-line text.
Expected outcome: Correct account and actual time appear once; matching outreach advances automatically. Text sender is the shared main line.

Steps: Salesperson asks champion to help with one prospect response; champion replies.
Expected outcome: One scoped help assignment; original due date and sales-manager accountability remain. The reply counts automatically; future lead work remains sales-owned.

Steps: Receive separate requests for two associations using one property-manager contact.
Expected outcome: Ambiguous activity is assigned for review. The system does not guess from a shared number or satisfy the other association's work.

Steps: Switch Front conversations while a draft preparation or edit is still pending.
Expected outcome: No draft or save lands on the wrong account/conversation.

Steps: Delay or replay a captured event using administrator tools in staging.
Expected outcome: Replayed activity does not duplicate outreach, move dates backwards or clear a newer unanswered request.

Steps: Assign two salespeople to different sales managers and the same champion. Let one sales deadline pass.
Expected outcome: Only the appropriate manager receives that sales escalation. The champion is not the sales fallback.

Steps: Leave sales work overdue.
Expected outcome: Manager receives escalation at 9 a.m. on the next business morning. If still unhandled after the manager's recovery day, owner receives it next business morning. Both keep visibility until work is handled.

Steps: Read/refresh the report or use “Handle this response.”
Expected outcome: Read/administrative actions do not complete work or reset the original deadline. Actual contact is the completion evidence.

Steps: Repeat with an overdue carrier or renewal obligation.
Expected outcome: Champion → marketing manager → owner; no sales-manager leakage.

Steps: Schedule temporary cover, change a manager, then end cover.
Expected outcome: Delivery follows current responsibility, dates stay unchanged, and work returns after cover ends. No self-manager or circular-cover choices.

Steps: Disable a responsible test identity or remove valid coverage.
Expected outcome: No send to a disabled user; valid cover/management or an owned exception remains. No silent missing work.

Steps: Give one person multiple eligible roles.
Expected outcome: At most one combined edition per person/environment/business date, without self-escalation duplicates.

Steps: Observe a real business-day 9 a.m. run.
Expected outcome: Salespeople and sales managers get one daily report, including a healthy zero. Champions/marketing managers/owner/exception owners receive editions when their scope requires attention.

Steps: Read each role's actual email.
Expected outcome: Why, next action, responsible name, due time, as-of time, counts, links and last relevant human contact are clear. AI email and mere inbound receipt are not mislabeled as human outreach.

Steps: Create more than 20 actionable items for one role in controlled fixtures.
Expected outcome: Email explicitly shows there are more items. Current report and CSV expose the full authorized scope.

Steps: Retry the report scheduler after a successful send.
Expected outcome: No second edition. A verified Front receipt marks delivery. Reading the report requires no acknowledgement.

Steps: Simulate an uncertain send in the engineering harness; review a corresponding staged case if needed.
Expected outcome: No blind resend. Admin can link the original sent Front message; the server checks the edition and recipient. Wrong message is rejected.

Steps: Inspect the internal reporting inbox and CRM communication history.
Expected outcome: Staff report messages never create prospect leads, satisfy outreach, or appear as client conversations.

Steps: Test a recipient outside the staging allowlist.
Expected outcome: Sending is blocked with an owned delivery issue. No message reaches that recipient.

Steps: Link a carrier conversation. Receive a carrier question.
Expected outcome: Champion gets carrier work. Existing client-side work remains distinct.

Steps: Correct an existing conversation from prospect to carrier/renewal context.
Expected outcome: Open correspondence moves to the correct role and policy. Original deadline and completed history remain intact.

Steps: Champion asks sales to obtain underwriting information. Sales sends the request.
Expected outcome: Sales outreach is recorded; the underlying information requirement remains. Follow-up stays at two business days while information is owed.

Steps: Send an informational prospect update while waiting only on carriers.
Expected outcome: It satisfies the weekly prospect update. It does not create an unnecessary two-day chase for a reply the prospect does not owe.

Steps: Add draft, submitted, declined, old-term and partial-coverage quotes.
Expected outcome: None falsely satisfies the usable-quote target. Correct term, policy, coverage, premium and offer validity matter.

Steps: Record a usable new-business quote. Prepare and actually send its quote email in Front.
Expected outcome: Sales presentation is due within one business day. Actual matching sent quote marks presentation; an abandoned draft does not.

Steps: Change quote terms after drafting, or remove its quoted facts from the draft before sending.
Expected outcome: It does not silently mark the revised quote as presented. Staff review the current quote; no fabricated completion.

Steps: Use Request binding on the approved quote; cancel once, then record actual client authorization in the normal quote flow.
Expected outcome: Cancel does nothing. Authorization creates champion bind work, without marking coverage bound or sending a carrier email by itself.

Steps: Send a carrier bind request; subsequently record confirmed binding through the existing bind form.
Expected outcome: Sending the request alone does not close the bind milestone. The actual policy closes it. Review begins within one business day and never after the coverage effective date.

Steps: Revise quoted terms after client authorization.
Expected outcome: Old authorization does not approve changed terms. Review/re-authorization is required; no silent bind on stale approval.

Steps: Bind one quote while another new-business quote remains open; then finish the remainder.
Expected outcome: Partial bind preserves remaining sales work. Final acquisition handoff stops ordinary lead chasing; champion becomes main client contact.

Steps: Bound client requests a certificate; champion acknowledges it.
Expected outcome: Response effort is recorded, but requested certificate delivery remains open.

Steps: Prepare the certificate through the request's button, then prepare its delivery email and send it in Front.
Expected outcome: File is tied to the actual request. Confirmed matching file delivery satisfies it. Creating a file or abandoning its email does not.

Steps: Repeat with a requested endorsement/policy document.
Expected outcome: Same principle: actual associated document and delivery evidence; an unrelated upload cannot clear it.

Steps: Champion assigns a specialist, who sends only an acknowledgement or forwards the request.
Expected outcome: Champion keeps client accountability. Assignment/acknowledgement does not pretend the requested result was delivered.

Steps: Complete a general service answer through normal correspondence.
Expected outcome: Substantive answer can satisfy correspondence; a no-answer attempt or “I'll check” does not. Specific document/bind requirements retain their stronger evidence rules.

Steps: Use a real policy term 90 days from the test date; allow the source-data sweep to run.
Expected outcome: Champion has renewal preparation. Empty generated records alone do not say preparation was done.

Steps: Send the needed renewal-information request or record an actual carrier submission.
Expected outcome: Initiation is satisfied; remaining information, submission, quote and bind work remains independently tracked.

Steps: Check carrier-specific submission requirements and a policy 14 days from expiration.
Expected outcome: Carrier deadlines drive submissions; usable-quote target is 14 calendar days before expiration. Missing lines/ambiguous terms are owned exceptions.

Steps: Let the client or carrier owe renewal information.
Expected outcome: Champion gets two-business-day follow-up. Marketing manager, then owner, handle missed obligations.

Steps: Test no eligible carrier, expired term and ambiguous renewal quotes.
Expected outcome: Placement/context exception remains visible; no false all-clear or arbitrary policy match.

Steps: Lead incumbent expiration is December 1, 2026. Choose Next year and confirm the displayed dates.
Expected outcome: Incumbent becomes December 1, 2027; salesperson returns September 2, 2027 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Source/owners/history stay intact.

Steps: Double-submit/retry the same rollover; separately edit the date concurrently.
Expected outcome: One calendar-year move only. Conflicting edit is rejected for review.

Steps: Keep an unanswered request or authorized bind requirement open while deferring ordinary chasing.
Expected outcome: Independent work remains tracked. Rollover does not change issued policy dates or erase requests.

Steps: Change salesperson during the deferred year, then reach return morning.
Expected outcome: Current salesperson receives outreach; no new automated introduction; normal cadence resumes from actual contact.

Steps: Test leap day, weekend/holiday, missing expiration and stale expiration.
Expected outcome: Feb 29 clamps to Feb 28; return uses the preceding business morning where needed. Missing date is requested; stale + one year does not secretly jump several years.

Steps: Use an old active account absent from the due queue.
Expected outcome: Full account census finds missing work or raises a named exception. A due-index-only check is insufficient.

Steps: Interrupt the worker, a provider request or a database write in engineering fixtures.
Expected outcome: Work remains durable; retries do not cancel it. Incomplete coverage is visible and independent monitoring detects the failure.

Steps: Disconnect the operations alert destination in a controlled setup check.
Expected outcome: Readiness fails; a CloudWatch alarm without a confirmed recipient is not accepted as an operating alert path.

Steps: Test Friday/holiday/DST and an existing 5 p.m. business deadline.
Expected outcome: Scheduled work arrives in the 9 a.m. Eastern window. Real deadlines and escalation recovery days remain correct.

Steps: Test all website form variants and retry a failed edited submission.
Expected outcome: One valid intake per submission; editable retries recover; readable Front brief and initial AI thread behavior remain intact.

Steps: Create leads from Google Ad Website, Organic Website, Phone, Email, Meta Ad and Property Manager.
Expected outcome: Correct source choices; source is set at creation, then protected. Organic and ad website attribution remain distinct.

Steps: View lead work and activity.
Expected outcome: Last contact date/time is visible and accurately distinguishes relevant human effort. Provider IDs stay protected behind deliberate administrative editing.

Steps: Download each dashboard report with filters applied.
Expected outcome: Usable export matches the displayed report scope, including empty and larger results.

Steps: Check finance, licensing, invoices and existing policy screens.
Expected outcome: Existing functions and unrelated reminders still work. Only overlapping sales/marketing report sections are consolidated.
